preguntas.pregunta: Could you tell us a little about yourself?
preguntas.pista_es: Presentación breve y ordenada (formación, experiencia, intereses), en 1–2 minutos, sin leer.
ideas: my academic background and where I studied
my professional experience so far, if any
my interests outside work: languages, travel, reading
repreguntas: What do you enjoy doing in your free time?

preguntas.pregunta: What did you study, and why did you choose that subject?
preguntas.pista_es: Explicar la carrera y una o dos razones personales de la elección; enlazar con la oposición.
ideas: an early interest in how the economy works
the wish to understand public policy and international trade
a degree that opens many professional doors
repreguntas: Which subject did you find most difficult at university?

preguntas.pregunta: How have you been preparing for this exam, and what has been the most difficult part?
preguntas.pista_es: Describir el método de estudio y reconocer una dificultad real con la forma en que se ha superado.
ideas: a daily routine with a tutor and regular oral presentations
the sheer volume of the syllabus and the need for constant revision
staying motivated over a long period and managing stress
repreguntas: What would you do differently if you had to start again?
How do you organise your revision?

preguntas.pregunta: What experience do you have of living abroad or working in an international environment?
preguntas.pista_es: Contar una experiencia concreta y lo que se aprendió de ella; si no se tiene, hablar de contactos internacionales o del plan de adquirirla.
ideas: an exchange semester or summer course abroad
working in a team with people from different countries
learning to adapt to different ways of working and communicating
repreguntas: What surprised you most about that experience?

preguntas.pregunta: Where and how did you learn English?
preguntas.pista_es: Relatar el aprendizaje del idioma y cómo se mantiene ahora (lectura, podcasts, conversación).
ideas: at school and later with private classes or an academy
stays in English-speaking countries
reading the press and listening to podcasts every day
repreguntas: What do you find most difficult about English?

preguntas.pregunta: Which part of the syllabus have you found most interesting, and why?
preguntas.pista_es: Elegir un tema concreto y justificar el interés con argumentos, mostrando dominio del contenido.
ideas: international trade theory and its relevance to current trade tensions
the economics of the European Union and the euro
development economics and the role of institutions
repreguntas: Is there any part of the syllabus that you would change or update?

preguntas.pregunta: Why do you want to become a Técnico Comercial y Economista del Estado?
preguntas.pista_es: Motivación personal y profesional clara: servicio público, economía internacional, carrera en el exterior.
ideas: the chance to serve the public interest using economic knowledge
the international dimension of the job
the variety of positions throughout a career
repreguntas: When did you first hear about this profession?

preguntas.pregunta: What do you think the daily work of an Economic and Commercial Counsellor at an embassy involves?
preguntas.pista_es: Describir las funciones de una Oficina Económica y Comercial: apoyo a empresas, análisis económico, relaciones institucionales.
ideas: supporting Spanish companies that want to enter the local market
analysing the host country's economy and reporting to Madrid
maintaining contacts with local authorities and business associations
promoting Spain as a destination for investment
repreguntas: Which of those tasks do you think would be the most challenging?
In which country would you like to work, and why?

preguntas.pregunta: Would you be willing to spend a large part of your career abroad? What challenges would that involve?
preguntas.pista_es: Respuesta sincera y madura: disposición, retos personales y profesionales y cómo afrontarlos.
ideas: adapting to new cultures, languages and ways of doing business
the impact on family and personal life
the professional enrichment of seeing different economic systems at first hand
repreguntas: How would you prepare for a posting in a country whose language you do not speak?

preguntas.pregunta: In which area of the administration would you like to work first, and why?
preguntas.pista_es: Elegir un destino (política comercial, financiación internacional, análisis macroeconómico, red exterior…) y argumentar.
ideas: trade policy, because of the current debates on tariffs and trade agreements
international finance and relations with multilateral institutions
the network of Economic and Commercial Offices abroad
repreguntas: What skills from your background would be most useful there?

preguntas.pregunta: What qualities do you think a good civil servant working on international economic affairs needs?
preguntas.pista_es: Enumerar y justificar cualidades (rigor técnico, idiomas, negociación, integridad…) con ejemplos.
ideas: sound technical knowledge and analytical rigour
negotiation and communication skills in several languages
integrity and a sense of public service
flexibility and the ability to adapt quickly
repreguntas: Which of these qualities do you think you need to develop most?

preguntas.pregunta: Some people argue that the public sector can no longer compete with the private sector to attract talent. What would you say to them?
preguntas.pista_es: Matizar: reconocer las diferencias salariales y argumentar otras ventajas del sector público y posibles mejoras.
ideas: salaries may be lower, but the work offers a unique sense of purpose and responsibility
public employment offers variety, stability and international mobility
the administration could improve talent attraction through flexibility and professional development
repreguntas: What would you change to make the public sector more attractive to young graduates?

preguntas.pregunta: What is inflation, and why do central banks try to keep it at around 2 %?
preguntas.pista_es: Definir la inflación y explicar el objetivo (margen frente a la deflación, sesgos de medición, anclaje de expectativas).
ideas: inflation is a sustained rise in the general level of prices
a small positive rate provides a safety margin against deflation
a clear target helps to anchor expectations
repreguntas: What are the costs of very high inflation?
And why is deflation considered dangerous?

preguntas.pregunta: How does a rise in interest rates affect households and businesses?
preguntas.pista_es: Explicar los canales de transmisión: crédito, hipotecas a tipo variable, ahorro, inversión.
ideas: mortgage and loan repayments increase, especially at variable rates
saving becomes more attractive and consumption falls
firms postpone investment projects because financing is more expensive
repreguntas: Are all countries in the euro area affected in the same way?

preguntas.pregunta: What are the main limits of fiscal policy in a country with high public debt?
preguntas.pista_es: Analizar el espacio fiscal: coste de la deuda, reglas fiscales, confianza de los mercados, sostenibilidad.
ideas: higher debt means more spending on interest payments
markets may demand a risk premium
European fiscal rules restrict deficits and set debt-reduction paths
the composition of spending and revenue matters as much as the overall balance
repreguntas: How would you reduce public debt without harming growth?

preguntas.pregunta: In your opinion, how well have fiscal and monetary policy been coordinated in the euro area in recent years?
preguntas.pista_es: Valoración matizada con ejemplos de fases (crisis de deuda, pandemia, inflación posterior).
ideas: during the debt crisis, fiscal austerity and monetary policy pulled in different directions
during the pandemic, both policies acted together on a large scale
the lack of a central fiscal capacity makes coordination difficult
repreguntas: Should the euro area have a common budget?

preguntas.pregunta: Why has productivity growth been so weak in many advanced economies?
preguntas.pista_es: Mencionar varias explicaciones posibles (difusión tecnológica, inversión, capital humano, competencia, medición) sin dar cifras inventadas.
ideas: new technologies spread slowly from leading firms to the rest of the economy
investment, particularly in intangible assets, has been insufficient
a shift towards services where productivity gains are harder to achieve
measurement problems in the digital economy
repreguntas: What could Spain do to raise its productivity?

preguntas.pregunta: Should central banks take climate change or inequality into account when making decisions?
preguntas.pista_es: Debatir mandato frente a independencia: riesgos financieros del clima, efectos distributivos de la política monetaria, legitimidad democrática.
ideas: climate change creates financial risks that affect price and financial stability
monetary policy has distributional effects, whether intended or not
broadening the mandate could threaten central bank independence
these goals are primarily the responsibility of elected governments
repreguntas: Who should decide on the mandate of a central bank?

preguntas.pregunta: What role do Spain's Economic and Commercial Offices abroad play?
preguntas.pista_es: Describir su función en la red exterior y en la internacionalización de la empresa española.
ideas: they provide information and personalised services to Spanish exporters
they analyse the economy and trade policy of the host country
they help to attract foreign investment to Spain
they represent Spain's economic interests before local authorities
repreguntas: How could their services be improved?

preguntas.pregunta: What are the main difficulties a small Spanish company faces when it starts exporting?
preguntas.pista_es: Identificar obstáculos (información, financiación, tamaño, idiomas, normativa) y apoyos disponibles.
ideas: lack of information about foreign markets and regulations
small size and limited financial resources
language barriers and a lack of international staff
the cost and risk of the first steps abroad
repreguntas: Which public instruments exist to help them?

preguntas.pregunta: What are the consequences of tariffs for the country that imposes them?
preguntas.pista_es: Explicar efectos sobre precios, consumidores, empresas que usan insumos importados, represalias y eficiencia.
ideas: higher prices for consumers and firms that use imported inputs
protected sectors may gain, but at a cost to the rest of the economy
the risk of retaliation against the country's exporters
less pressure to innovate in protected industries
repreguntas: Can tariffs ever be justified?

preguntas.pregunta: Trade policy is an exclusive competence of the European Union. What room for manoeuvre does a member state like Spain have?
preguntas.pista_es: Explicar el reparto de competencias y cómo influye un Estado miembro (Consejo, negociación de mandatos, promoción comercial nacional).
ideas: member states shape the Commission's negotiating mandates in the Council
Spain can defend its interests through alliances with other member states
export promotion and support for internationalisation remain national
the EU's size gives Spain more negotiating power than it would have alone
repreguntas: Can you think of an area where Spain's interests differ from those of other member states?

preguntas.pregunta: Do you think the World Trade Organization is still relevant today?
preguntas.pista_es: Valoración equilibrada: funciones de la OMC, crisis del órgano de apelación, dificultades de negociación multilateral.
ideas: it still provides the basic rules on which most world trade is based
its dispute settlement system has been weakened
multilateral negotiations have made little progress, so countries turn to bilateral agreements
reform is needed rather than abandonment
repreguntas: What reforms would you propose?

preguntas.pregunta: Is the trend towards nearshoring and «friend-shoring» a threat or an opportunity for Spain?
preguntas.pista_es: Analizar la reconfiguración de las cadenas de valor y la posición de España (ubicación, energía, costes, mercado único).
ideas: companies are seeking shorter, more secure supply chains
Spain could attract investment thanks to its location, its renewable energy and its membership of the single market
fragmentation of world trade could reduce overall efficiency and raise prices
the outcome depends on infrastructure, skills and regulatory stability
repreguntas: Which sectors could benefit most?
What should public policy do to attract this investment?

preguntas.pregunta: What does the European Union mean to you personally?
preguntas.pista_es: Respuesta personal con ejemplos cotidianos (viajar, estudiar, trabajar, moneda común).
ideas: the freedom to travel, study and work in other countries
using the same currency in many countries
a project of peace and cooperation
repreguntas: Have you ever benefited directly from a European programme?

preguntas.pregunta: What are the main advantages of the single market for Spanish companies?
preguntas.pista_es: Explicar las cuatro libertades y su efecto en las empresas (tamaño del mercado, armonización, competencia).
ideas: access to a market of hundreds of millions of consumers without tariffs
common rules and standards that reduce costs
easier access to suppliers, capital and workers
greater competition that encourages efficiency
repreguntas: Are there still barriers within the single market?

preguntas.pregunta: What has the euro meant for Spain?
preguntas.pista_es: Ventajas (estabilidad, tipos bajos, comercio) e inconvenientes (pérdida del tipo de cambio, crisis), con conclusión propia.
ideas: price stability and lower interest rates
no exchange-rate risk in trade with other euro area countries
the loss of the exchange rate as an adjustment tool
the need for flexibility and competitiveness through other means
repreguntas: Would Spain be better off outside the euro?

preguntas.pregunta: What are the EU's main challenges in terms of competitiveness compared with the United States and China?
preguntas.pista_es: Tocar innovación, tamaño de empresas, mercado de capitales, energía y regulación, sin cifras inventadas.
ideas: lower investment in research and new technologies
fragmented capital markets that make it harder for start-ups to grow
higher energy costs
regulation that can be complex, although it also protects citizens
repreguntas: What should be the EU's priority to close this gap?

preguntas.pregunta: Should the European Union continue to enlarge? What would the consequences be for a country like Spain?
preguntas.pista_es: Argumentar a favor y en contra (geopolítica, presupuesto, fondos de cohesión, toma de decisiones) y concluir.
ideas: enlargement strengthens stability and the EU's weight in the world
it would change the distribution of cohesion and agricultural funds
decision-making with more members would require institutional reform
new members can also offer new markets for Spanish companies
repreguntas: Which reforms would be necessary before further enlargement?

preguntas.pregunta: Should decisions on foreign policy or taxation continue to require unanimity in the Council?
preguntas.pista_es: Debate entre eficacia y soberanía; mencionar alternativas (mayoría cualificada, cooperación reforzada).
ideas: unanimity protects national sovereignty in sensitive areas
it allows a single member state to block decisions
qualified majority voting would make the EU more effective
enhanced cooperation allows some countries to move forward first
repreguntas: Would Spain gain or lose from the end of unanimity?

preguntas.pregunta: What do you do in your daily life to save energy or protect the environment?
preguntas.pista_es: Ejemplos personales sencillos y una reflexión breve sobre la responsabilidad individual y colectiva.
ideas: using public transport or cycling instead of the car
recycling and reducing waste
saving energy at home
repreguntas: Do you think individual actions are enough?

preguntas.pregunta: How will artificial intelligence change the way we work?
preguntas.pista_es: Efectos sobre tareas, empleos y cualificaciones; oportunidades y riesgos.
ideas: automation of routine tasks, including some office tasks
new jobs and new skills will be needed
productivity could rise, but the gains may be unevenly distributed
the importance of training throughout working life
repreguntas: Could AI be useful in the work of an Economic and Commercial Office?

preguntas.pregunta: Why is it so difficult for young people to buy or rent a home in big cities?
preguntas.pista_es: Causas (oferta, demanda, alquiler turístico, salarios) y posibles soluciones.
ideas: supply of housing has not kept up with demand
jobs are concentrated in large cities
short-term rentals reduce the supply for residents
wages for young people have grown slowly
repreguntas: Are rent controls a good solution?

preguntas.pregunta: What are the economic consequences of population ageing, and how can they be addressed?
preguntas.pista_es: Pensiones, sanidad, mercado laboral, crecimiento; respuestas (empleo, inmigración, productividad, reformas).
ideas: pressure on pension and health systems
a smaller working-age population and labour shortages
possible lower growth unless productivity increases
responses: raising employment rates, immigration, longer working lives
repreguntas: Should the retirement age be linked to life expectancy?

preguntas.pregunta: Is the energy transition compatible with industrial competitiveness?
preguntas.pista_es: Costes a corto plazo frente a ventajas a largo plazo; caso de España (renovables).
ideas: in the short term, the transition requires major investment and may raise costs
in the long term, renewables can provide cheaper and more secure energy
Spain has a comparative advantage in solar and wind power
support is needed for the sectors and regions most affected
repreguntas: What role should green hydrogen play?

preguntas.pregunta: What role should immigration play in addressing labour shortages in ageing societies?
preguntas.pista_es: Respuesta matizada: necesidades del mercado de trabajo, integración, efectos fiscales, debate social.
ideas: immigration can fill shortages in specific sectors
successful integration requires language training, recognition of qualifications and housing
its fiscal impact depends on employment rates
it is a complement to, not a substitute for, other policies such as raising productivity
repreguntas: How could the recognition of foreign qualifications be improved?

preguntas.pregunta: If a foreign friend visited Spain for the first time, which region would you recommend, and why?
preguntas.pista_es: Descripción atractiva y personal de una región (paisaje, gastronomía, cultura).
ideas: the landscapes and the climate
the food and local traditions
the history and monuments
repreguntas: And what would you advise them to avoid?

preguntas.pregunta: What are the main strengths of the Spanish economy?
preguntas.pista_es: Enumerar fortalezas sin datos inventados: turismo, exportaciones diversificadas, infraestructuras, renovables, multinacionales.
ideas: a world-leading tourism sector
a diversified export base, from food to cars and services
modern transport infrastructure
great potential in renewable energy
repreguntas: And what are its main weaknesses?

preguntas.pregunta: How important is tourism for the Spanish economy, and what are its risks?
preguntas.pista_es: Peso del turismo (empleo, divisas) y riesgos (dependencia, estacionalidad, vivienda, medio ambiente).
ideas: a major source of employment and foreign currency
dependence on a sector vulnerable to external shocks
seasonal and often low-paid jobs
pressure on housing and natural resources in some areas
repreguntas: How could Spain diversify its tourism model?

preguntas.pregunta: Why has unemployment in Spain traditionally been higher than in other European countries?
preguntas.pista_es: Explicaciones estructurales: dualidad del mercado laboral, estructura productiva, formación, ciclos.
ideas: a high share of temporary contracts that makes employment very sensitive to the cycle
a productive structure with many sectors dependent on demand cycles, such as construction and tourism
mismatches between education and the needs of employers
recent labour reforms have tried to reduce temporary employment
repreguntas: What effect have recent labour reforms had, in your view?

preguntas.pregunta: Which Spanish sectors have the greatest potential for internationalisation?
preguntas.pista_es: Elegir varios sectores y justificar con ventajas competitivas.
ideas: the agri-food sector, with a strong reputation abroad
infrastructure and engineering, where Spanish firms are global players
renewable energy
tourism services and fashion
repreguntas: What role can public institutions play in supporting them?

preguntas.pregunta: How would you explain the differences in income and productivity between Spanish regions?
preguntas.pista_es: Factores (estructura productiva, capital humano, urbanización, historia, infraestructuras) y políticas de convergencia.
ideas: differences in productive structure and specialisation
the concentration of skilled workers and firms in large urban areas
different levels of education and innovation
the role of regional policy and European cohesion funds
repreguntas: Have European funds helped regions to converge?

preguntas.pregunta: Should all university students spend a year abroad?
preguntas.pista_es: Opinión clara con dos o tres argumentos y un contraargumento.
ideas: it improves language skills and independence
it opens students' minds to other cultures
but it is expensive, so financial help is necessary
repreguntas: Would you have liked to spend more time abroad?

preguntas.pregunta: Should working from home be a right for all employees whose job allows it?
preguntas.pista_es: Ventajas e inconvenientes para trabajadores y empresas, y conclusión matizada.
ideas: better work-life balance and less commuting
possible isolation and less learning from colleagues
companies need flexibility to organise their work
hybrid models may offer a balance
repreguntas: Does remote work have any effect on regional development?

preguntas.pregunta: Should the working week be reduced to four days?
preguntas.pista_es: Argumentos (productividad, bienestar, costes, sectores) y opinión justificada.
ideas: it could improve well-being and motivation
it may be difficult for small businesses and some sectors
its success depends on productivity gains
trials could be carried out before any general reform
repreguntas: Who should decide: governments or social partners?

preguntas.pregunta: Should rich countries tax wealth more heavily?
preguntas.pista_es: Debate: equidad, recaudación, fuga de capitales, competencia fiscal, alternativas.
ideas: wealth is more concentrated than income
wealth taxes may raise little revenue and encourage capital flight
international cooperation is needed to avoid tax competition
taxes on inheritance or on capital income are alternatives
repreguntas: What do you think of international agreements on minimum taxation?

preguntas.pregunta: Should governments subsidise strategic industries such as semiconductors or batteries?
preguntas.pista_es: Política industrial: argumentos de seguridad y externalidades frente a riesgos de ineficiencia y carrera de subsidios.
ideas: supply security and strategic autonomy
the risk of choosing the wrong winners and wasting public money
subsidy races between the EU, the United States and China
the need for clear conditions and evaluation
repreguntas: Should these subsidies be decided at national or at European level?

preguntas.pregunta: Should economic growth remain the main objective of economic policy?
preguntas.pista_es: Debate sobre crecimiento, bienestar, sostenibilidad e indicadores alternativos, con postura argumentada.
ideas: growth finances public services and reduces poverty
GDP does not measure well-being, inequality or environmental damage
the goal could be sustainable and inclusive growth
alternative indicators can complement GDP
repreguntas: Is «degrowth» a realistic option for advanced economies?

preguntas.pregunta: Have you ever been to an English-speaking country? What impressed you most?
preguntas.pista_es: Relato personal sencillo; si no se ha viajado, hablar del país que se querría visitar y por qué.
ideas: the people and their way of life
the cities, landscapes or museums
the differences in food and daily habits
repreguntas: Would you like to live there?

preguntas.pregunta: Is there a book, film or series in English that you particularly like?
preguntas.pista_es: Presentar una obra y explicar por qué gusta; vocabulario de opinión.
ideas: what the story is about
why it impressed you
how it helped you to improve your English
repreguntas: Do you prefer watching films in the original version?

preguntas.pregunta: What do you know about the economic relationship between Spain and the United Kingdom?
preguntas.pista_es: Vínculos (turismo, inversión, comercio, residentes) sin cifras inventadas; efecto del Brexit.
ideas: the United Kingdom is one of the main sources of tourists to Spain
there are significant mutual investments, for example in banking, infrastructure and telecommunications
many British citizens live in Spain and many Spaniards in the United Kingdom
Brexit has added new barriers to trade
repreguntas: How has Brexit affected Spanish companies?

preguntas.pregunta: In your opinion or experience, what are the main differences between the British and the Spanish way of working?
preguntas.pista_es: Comparación respetuosa, evitando tópicos rígidos; horarios, comunicación, reuniones.
ideas: different working hours and lunch habits
communication styles: more direct or more indirect
attitudes to punctuality and planning
these are generalisations and every organisation is different
repreguntas: What could each country learn from the other?

preguntas.pregunta: Why has English become the global language of business, and will it keep this position?
preguntas.pista_es: Causas históricas y económicas y perspectivas (otras lenguas, tecnología de traducción).
ideas: the historical influence of the British Empire and later of the United States
the dominance of English in science, technology and finance
the growing importance of other languages such as Chinese or Spanish
automatic translation may change the role of a lingua franca
repreguntas: What is the international position of Spanish?

preguntas.pregunta: What have been the economic consequences of Brexit for the United Kingdom and for the EU?
preguntas.pista_es: Valoración sin cifras inventadas: comercio, inversión, migración, servicios financieros, relación futura.
ideas: new customs formalities and barriers to trade in goods and services
uncertainty that affected investment
changes in labour migration and shortages in some sectors
the EU lost an important member, but maintained its unity during the negotiations
repreguntas: Do you think the United Kingdom will move closer to the EU again?
